\begin{abstract}
Likert and pairwise scoring produce consistently divergent sensitivity across tested surface-level style axes when applied to LLM judges.
We introduce Controlled Style Decomposition (CSD), a black-box diagnostic methodology that quantifies this divergence under controlled conditions via human-validated, NLI-gated content control, per-axis style decomposition, and position-controlled pairwise comparison.

Likert and pairwise scoring produce divergent sensitivity across two primary and one exploratory surface-level style axis, with varying effect sizes across judges, when applied to LLM judges.
We define this divergence---the \emph{Likert Blindspot}---operationally as statistically significant pairwise sensitivity absent from Likert, without committing to a specific causal mechanism; it admits non-exclusive explanations including measurement attenuation, format amplification, and construct divergence.
